note: The NIST WebBook publishes NO Shomate polynomial for gas-phase methanol, only the tabulated ideal-gas heat capacity compiled by Thermodynamics Research Center (1997) at p = 1 bar, plus the enthalpy-of-formation entries below. This file stores those values verbatim; nothing is fitted to them by this project.
cp_comment: Thermodynamics Research Center, 1997 (GT compilation): 'Recommended entropies and heat capacities are in good agreement with other statistically calculated values' [Ivash 1955, Zhuravlev 1959, Chen 1977, Chao 1986, Gurvich/Veyts 1989]. 44.06 +/- 0.03 J/mol/K at 298.15 K.

dHf_gas_298_kJ_per_mol.used_from: printed on the same NIST page as the Rossini (1932) combustion result: 'dHf(gas) = -201.49 kJ/mol (simple calculation by NIST; no Washburn corrections); ALS'
dHf_gas_298_kJ_per_mol.alternative_from: 'AVG, average of 9 values' in the page header
dHf_gas_298_kJ_per_mol.why_this_one: -201.49 kJ/mol reproduces BOTH reaction enthalpies already cited in this project (Appl. Sci. 2017 7,1213): CO2 + 3H2 -> CH3OH + H2O gives -49.8 vs -49.7 kJ/mol and CO + 2H2 -> CH3OH gives -91.0 vs -90.7 kJ/mol. The -205 value is carried as a sensitivity (it shifts the adiabatic rise by about 4 K on the VBF base case).

integration.method: trapezoid on the tabulated grid, piecewise-linear Cp between points; enthalpy reference 298.15 K
integration.discretisation_check: trapezoid on the published grid vs the same piecewise-linear Cp integrated on a 400-point midpoint grid: 0.0005 J/mol over 298.15-600 K (relative 2.9e-8) - exact for linear segments, measured by model/methanol_converter.py cp_integration_error()
